transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Evan (Redwood SE), Aisha (Head of AI, Sparrow), Carlos (Platform Eng), Lina (Security Lead), Devon (PM)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick audio check? Can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Aisha (Sparrow): Yeah loud and clear, thanks.
[00:08] Carlos: yep good here.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. So agenda — quick intro, we'll run through the onboarding playbook, cover security and perf expectations, and assign owners. Any burning items to add?
[00:22] Devon: Nothing extra from product side, mostly alignment on SLOs and timeline.
[00:27] Maya (Redwood CSM): I'll take notes on the sprint plan and follow up with calendar invites.
[00:31] Jordan: Awesome. Quick intros — Jordan AE, Maya CSM, Evan SE — Evan is going to run the benchmarks and help with deployment choices.
[00:38] Evan (Redwood SE): Hi all, hi. I'll be tagging into infra bits and perf.
[00:42] Aisha: I'm Aisha, I own the ML platform at Sparrow. We're trying to get Redwood in for chat and embedding endpoints for our customer-facing assistant.
[00:50] Carlos: Carlos, infra. We're responsible for VPC, KMS, and CI.
[00:54] Lina: Lina, security — SOC2 lead, data residency questions.
[00:58] Jordan: Cool. High-level goal from your kickoff docs was to get to a pilot by end of April and production in Q2. Is that still the target?
[01:06] Aisha: Yes, ideally pilot late April. Production by mid-May if all goes well.
[01:10] Devon: We can be flexible but timeline is important for a customer launch.
[01:14] Jordan: Understood. On success criteria you listed latency p95 < 150ms and a cost target roughly 40% below current on-prem ops. Is that correct? (paraphrase)
[01:22] Aisha: That's right. Cost per 1M tokens is our baseline and low-latency for interactive flows.
[01:28] Jordan: Great. Let's walk the onboarding playbook — Maya, can you pull up the runbook briefly?
[01:34] Maya: Yep, I'm putting the runbook link in the chat. (link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/sparrow-onboard) Sorry the link in transcript may be truncated.
[01:44] Jordan: The playbook has two-week sprints, clear milestones: credentials & access, test dataset ingestion, perf baseline, then pilot cutover. We'll propose weekly 30-minute check-ins for the first six weeks.
[01:55] Devon: Weekly check-ins sound good. Can we add a weekly perf digest?
[01:58] Evan: We can push a short report after each benchmark run — latency distributions, token counts, and cost estimates.
[02:04] Carlos: For infra, we need IP allowlist details and guidance on VPC peering; also any infra-as-code snippets would help.
[02:12] Evan: We'll share Terraform snippets for the VPC peering and example endpoint configs. They worked in several customers, though sometimes names are off in the docs, so check variables.
[02:22] Lina: On security, two quick asks: 1) what is the SOC2 coverage for Redwood Private vs Hosted? and 2) how is customer data encrypted at rest — do we integrate with our KMS?
[02:33] Jordan: Good questions. Short answer: Redwood has SOC 2 at org level for hosted; for Private deployments we can document scope and integrate with customer KMS/HSM. I'll send the SOC2 summary and an options doc after the call.
[02:45] Maya: Adding note — Lina will need our security questionnaire and SSO/SAML flows. We'll attach the security zip.
[02:51] Aisha: Also curious about model rollback and canary rollouts — we run A/B tests and want safe fallback in case of regressions.
[02:59] Evan: The platform supports canary rollouts by percentage and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant if quality drops. We can show patterns in a demo.
[03:08] Carlos: Perf — baseline numbers matter. What dataset size and token lengths should we use? Our assistant median is about 280 tokens per request, with heavy tail to 1.2k.
[03:18] Evan: Good. For the initial benchmark we'll test median 256/512 windows and a 1k tail sample. We'll report p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
[03:27] Jordan: Aisha, do you have a dev dataset we can use or do you want Redwood to generate synthetic traffic?
[03:33] Aisha: We can export a 5k-sample dev corpus, sanitized. Carlos will coordinate the export.
[03:38] Carlos: Yep, I'll drop a GCS link and creds for a temporary bucket.
[03:42] Lina: Quick sec — data residency, some customers' PII can't leave EU. We'll need confirmation on region pinning for endpoints.
[03:50] Jordan: Yes region pinning is supported; we'll document region availability and options for Dedicated or Private if EU-only required.
[03:58] Devon: About costs — are there levers we can use to hit the 40% reduction? Batching? Quantization?
[04:04] Evan: Yes. Redwood Optimize recommendations include quantization profiles, batching, prefix cache, and routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical paths. We'll propose a config in the cost estimate.
[04:14] Aisha: Great. Can that be part of the pilot — test a quantized variant in a canary?
[04:19] Evan: Yes — we can run a parallel route with lower-cost quantized model for 10% of traffic.
[04:24] Jordan: Ok, timeline: Week 1 (access, dataset ingest, infra snippets), Week 2 (benchmarks, playbook adjustments), Week 3 (pilot launch). Does that map to end of April pilot?
[04:35] Devon: Yes if we start next week.
[04:38] Maya: I'll propose sprint calendar with milestones and owners.
[04:43] Aisha: For legal/compliance, procurement needs a list of standard terms. Who owns getting that to our procurement team?
[04:50] Jordan: I'll loop in Redwood legal and provide an initial SOW template. Procurement contact?
[04:55] Devon: I'll share procurement contact after the call.
[04:58] Jordan: Quick note on observability — Console will give token-level cost and per-route latency; we'll give you a sample dashboard and tracing hooks.
[05:07] Carlos: Hook details are helpful. We want to integrate with Datadog, OpenTelemetry.
[05:12] Evan: We have built-in tracing connectors and can push to your Datadog instance; we will include an example config in the runbook.
[05:20] Aisha: Any constraints we should raise now? For example, we use Strict CSP and some of our web integrations block external scripts.
[05:28] Jordan: Our backend calls the API server-side so CSP shouldn't be a blocker; we can provide server-side SDK examples.
[05:35] Lina: For SSO we require SCIM and SAML. Is SCIM supported?
[05:39] Maya: Yes, SCIM provisioning is supported for users and groups in hosted; for Private we'll provide entitlement mapping docs.
[05:47] Aisha: Let's talk about escalation paths if we hit perf or security blockers mid-pilot.
[05:52] Jordan: We'll set aside an S1/S2 escalation contact list. I'll include on-call rotation and SE contact in the runbook.
[05:58] Devon: On instrumentation, we'd like a lightweight heatmap of token costs by intent to prioritize optimization. Is that something Redwood Console can show?
[06:08] Evan: Yes — token-level breakdowns and per-route economics are available; we can add intent tags. You'll need to add a small header in the request to surface intent.
[06:16] Aisha: OK. Any blockers for infra to start?
[06:20] Carlos: We'll need example IAM roles and the Terraform snippets, plus a timeframe for the temporary credentials.
[06:27] Evan: We'll provide example IAM roles and a template TF module; credentials can be scoped for two weeks during the pilot.
[06:33] Jordan: All right, quick demo? Evan, do a screen share to show the runbook and where the perf artifacts go.
[06:38] Evan: I don't have screen in the transcript but I'll describe: the runbook has a checklist, a terraform folder, and a perf folder with a sample JMeter script (names sometimes garbled in the export).
[06:49] Aisha: Sounds good. For stats, what does it take to get p95 under 150ms — GPU choice? Model selection?
[06:56] Evan: It's combination: 1) model variant with lower latency profile, 2) batching config tuned for interactive SLOs, and 3) prefilling/cache for hot prefixes. We'll include recommended hardware (A100 vs H100 tradeoffs) but you may want Dedicated for consistent tail latency.
[07:12] Carlos: Dedicated capacity is interesting but we need to understand commit levels and autoscale burst.
[07:18] Jordan: We'll provide Dedicated pricing and recommended commit for your traffic shape once we see the benchmark.
[07:23] Lina: Another security question — audit logs retention. We need 12 months for some customers. Can Redwood Console keep logs that long?
[07:31] Maya: We have extended retention as an add-on; we'll put options and pricing in the doc.
[07:36] Devon: Ok, wrapping into next steps and owners — Jordan?
[07:40] Jordan: Sure. Recap: Jordan to send runbook + SOC2 summary + Dedicated pricing options (due 4/9). Evan to run perf benchmark with the dev dataset once Carlos shares link (due 4/16). Maya to schedule weekly check-ins starting 4/14. Lina to deliver security questionnaire answers (due 4/12). Devon to share procurement contact. Any other items?
[07:59] Aisha: Can we also get a sample dashboard and the Terraform snippet earlier if possible?
[08:04] Evan: Yes, we'll prioritize the TF snippet and sample dashboard by 4/9 too.
[08:09] Carlos: I'll provision the GCS bucket today and send link to Evan.
[08:13] Jordan: Great. Any final Qs?
[08:16] Lina: One last — does Redwood support bringing your own model weights in Private?
[08:21] Evan: Yes, Private supports custom weights and we can help with kernel/quantization recommendations. There are nuances with licensing so we'll cover that in a follow-up doc.
[08:32] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook, calendar invites, and the security pack.
[08:36] Aisha: Thank you all, excited to get started.
[08:39] Jordan: End note — I'll include a link to the shared tracker and a short checklist in the email. Bye.

End transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "TF snippet" sometimes transcribed as "tee-eff snip") and run-on lines typical of auto-transcripts.
